author: TEDx Talks
description: We still think of digital technologies as products, but over the last couple of decades, first slowly then rapidly, they have become architectures, virtual spaces within which we live and work, and whose rules are established by their developers and owners. In this conversation, Bruno Giussani, former European director of TED and author of "Our Minds Under Siege: How to Avoid Being Manipulated in the Age of AI" and Katerina Biliouri, curator and co-founder of Lemondrop, discuss the meaning of this technological evolution for our lives and explore how AI, as the old Greeks would say, is a "pharmakon": at the same time remedy and poison, help and threat. Bruno Giussani is the author of "Our Minds Under Siege: How to Avoid Being Manipulated in the Age of artificial intelligence" (Scheidegger & Spiess, 2026) and the former European director and global curator of TED. He’s written for newspapers in Europe and the United States (including, for several years, an internet column for The New Y
title: We don’t buy digital products: We live in them | Bruno Giussani & Katerina Biliouri | TEDxBerlin

author: TEDx Talks
description: AI is not just changing tasks — it is changing how organizations hold together. Florian Bankoley argues that hierarchy was our old answer to complexity, but AI forces us to invent a new one. As intelligence and decision support spread across institutions, leaders must rethink trust, authority, coordination and legitimacy before old organizational structures stop holding. Florian Bankoley is Chief Digital Officer of Bosch Mobility, leading digital, AI, software, data, and IT transformation across one of the world’s largest mobility businesses. Over two decades, he has moved between corporate leadership, entrepreneurship, and board roles — including founding a digital mobility business within Bosch and driving major global transformation programs. Florian is fascinated by the human side of change: why some ideas scale, why others fail, and what leadership really demands in times of disruption. With roots across Europe and a career shaped by technology and business, he brings a practical
title: Why AI forces us to rethink leadership and organizations | Florian Bankoley | TEDxBerlin

author: TEDx Talks
description: Europe has spent two decades being told it is behind in AI. Entrepreneur Alexander Woellwarth-Lauterburg, who started inside the hidden human supply chain of the AI industry, argues we are measuring the wrong race entirely — and that the real competition is only just beginning. Alexander Woellwarth-Lauterburg is the founder and CEO of InnoButler, where he is building a sovereign European AI platform for enterprise R&D. He founded the company while working inside the hidden human supply chain of the AI industry — an experience that permanently demystified the technology for him. At the core of his work is a fascination with how knowledge moves: why some ideas travel across borders and industries while others get trapped, and what it costs a continent when its intelligence is built somewhere else. Alexander brings a grounded perspective on innovation, sovereignty, and the quiet decisions that shape who owns the future. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format
title: Why Europe was never behind in AI | Alexander Woellwarth-Lauterburg | TEDxBerlin

author: TEDx Talks
description: What should America strive to become over the next 250 years? Former U.S. Treasurer Rosa Rios, Chair of the America250 Commission, reflects on the nation's past while looking boldly toward its future. From her family's immigrant story to leading the national celebration of America's 250th anniversary, Rios shares a vision centered on opportunity, innovation, entrepreneurship, and civic engagement. She discusses empowering the next generation through initiatives like America's Startup, fostering patriotism through purpose, and creating new traditions of giving back. This inspiring conversation explores how innovation, education, and service can shape the next chapter of the American story. Rosie Rios was designated as the chair for the United States Semiquincentennial Commission in July 2022, following her prior appointment by Congress as one of the Commission’s 16 private citizens. From 2009 to 2016, Rios served as the 43rd Treasurer of the United States and just completed her term as
title: How America Can Inspire the Next Generation | Rosa Rios | TEDxBoston

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Who really decides what AI becomes? While governments debate regulation and companies race to build more powerful systems, communities are already shaping how artificial intelligence is adopted, trusted, and governed. Drawing on a decade spent building AI ecosystems across Europe, Elena Poughia challenges why the future of AI may be decided not by technology itself, but by the humans who organize around it. Elena Poughia is the founder of Data Natives, one of Europe's largest AI and data science communities, and Managing Director of Dataconomy, a leading global publication covering artificial intelligence and emerging technologies. For over a decade, she has worked at the intersection of technology, innovation, entrepreneurship, and community building, helping connect founders, researchers, policymakers, and investors across Europe and beyond. She serves on the SXSW Pitch Board and as an expert for the European Commission’s innovation programs.
In her talk, she explores why communitie
title: Why the future of AI will be decided by communities | Elena Poughia | TEDxBerlin

author: TEDx Talks
description: Rules are the foundation of democracy. But what happens when they become too complex for people, officials, and even institutions to apply? Drawing on her childhood in East Germany, the Dutch childcare-benefits scandal and her work with Rulemapping, Ina Remmers shows how AI can either deepen the crisis of trust in the state or help make democracy work again. Ina Remmers is an impact entrepreneur interested in how systems can strengthen social cohesion and democratic agency. She co-founded nebenan.de, Germany’s largest neighbourhood network, inspired by her own experience of growing up in small villages. Her work has been recognized by the German Startup Awards, where she was named Best Female Founder. Today, Remmers is the founder of the Rulemapping Group, where she works with her team to make laws and rules understandable, traceable and applicable for both people and machines. Her work focuses on building a citizen-focused state in which bureaucracy becomes a lever for trust, innovat
title: Why AI needs legal logic to strengthen democracy | Ina Remmers | TEDxBerlin

author: TEDx Talks
description: Every minute, somewhere in the world, a fall takes a life — and many are preventable. The data that could predict our decline is already streaming from our phones and wearables; the problem, says neuroscientist and inventor Dr. Cori Lathan, is that we've aimed AI at selling us shoes instead of keeping us alive. In this personal talk about her own parents, the hidden toll on caregivers, and the future she believes we can still choose, Lathan makes the case for finally pointing AI at the things that matters most. Dr. Corinna Lathan is an inventor, entrepreneur, and self-described future cyborg. Over three decades she's built technology to make humans stronger, smarter, and healthier. Her inventions sit at the intersection of science fiction and real-world impact — robots for kids with disabilities, brain-health tools for soldiers, virtual reality for astronauts, and wearables that turn electricity into medicine. She founded AnthroTronix, holds 35 patents, and wrote the bestseller, Inven
title: AI already tracks the data that could save lives | Cori Lathan | TEDxBerlin

author: TEDx Talks
description: AI didn't teach itself to think. We taught it through the messiness of our life struggles over millennia. Bright Simons introduces the Social Edge Paradox: the more we automate knowledge work, the more we starve AI of the civilisational substrate it needs to get smarter. He argues that the future of AI belongs not to Big Tech but to cross-thinkers - people like Bra Kofi in Africa's auto-garages, who can harness the tacit knowledge trapped in informal economies to advance AI that builds power plants instead of just PowerPoints. Bright Simons is a Ghanaian social innovator, writer, and policy thinker working at the intersection of technology, trust, and development. As President of mPedigree, he has helped deploy technologies across Africa and other regions to transform supply chains and consumer markets. He holds senior affiliations with top think tanks like IMANI and ODI Global and sits on many boards.Bright has advised organizations including Microsoft, the World Economic Forum, and
title: Cross-thinkers must inherit the world of AI | Bright Simons | TEDxBerlin

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What will Boston look like over the next 250 years?

In this conversation, veteran Boston Globe business reporter John Chesto explores the forces shaping the city's future—from AI and robotics to transportation, real estate, journalism, and economic development. Drawing on decades of reporting, he discusses how Boston can remain a global leader in innovation while adapting to changing technologies and industries.

From expanding innovation districts and electrifying public transit to the future of news and business leadership, this conversation offers a compelling look at what's next for one of the world's leading knowledge economies. Jon Chesto covers the leaders who shape Boston’s business community. He has been reporting on business and politics in New England for the past two decades. Before joining the Globe, he was managing editor at the Boston Business Journal. Prior to that role, he was the business editor at The Patriot Ledger in Quincy. His weekly Ledger column, “Mass. Marke
title: The Future of Boston: Business, AI, Infrastructure, and Innovation | Jon Chesto | TEDxBoston

author: TEDx Talks
description: Eric S. Rosenthal, MD, draws on Massachusetts’ revolutionary history to explore a new revolution in digital health and AI within medicine and neuroscience. Massachusetts was not merely the place where a new government began; it was a place where ordinary people built new systems for perceiving signals, sharing information, coordinating action, and imagining a different future. Two hundred and fifty years later, we are surrounded by signals again — in the pauses in a patient’s voice, the distance someone walks each day, the social networks they maintain, and the countless fragments of a medical record. Drawing from the breadth of digital and AI expertise at the Mass General Brigham Neuroscience Institute, the talk highlights how privacy-protecting, human-centered technologies — including ambient documentation, early diagnostic algorithms, voice and movement sensing, digital biomarkers, social and community mapping, predictive analytics, and monitoring that can help a clinician understa
title: The Humans Are Coming: AI in Neuroscience | Eric Rosenthal | TEDxBoston

title: The Truth About AGI | Otkrist Gupta | TEDxBoston

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What happens to human imagination when technology begins anticipating our thoughts before they fully form, reshaping our relationship with uncertainty, consequence, and irreversible time? Drawing from filmmaking, philosophy, and personal experience, director Marco Gentile explores how generative AI is reshaping not only creativity, but the conditions that make storytelling, freedom, and authorship possible in the first place. Marco Gentile is an Italian advertising, music videos and film director, writer, and speaker exploring storytelling, imagination, and human agency in the age of artificial intelligence. Known for his cinematic approach to commercial storytelling, he has directed international campaigns for brands including BMW, Mercedes-Benz, Adidas, Toyota, Vodafone, Lexus, and Coca-Cola, with work recognized at Cannes Lions and other major international festivals.

A Fulbright Scholar, Marco holds a Master’s degree in Film and Media Arts from Emerson College in Boston, as well
title: Imagination and storytelling in the age of AI | Marco Gentile | TEDxBerlin

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Every day, a billion new posts flood our feeds — and hidden among them, the fake news built to plant doubt. Entrepreneur Maxim Nitsche traces a real lie — that the Gates Foundation engineered ticks to stop us eating meat — as it travels from outlet to outlet in a single live visualization. Learn how AI has changed the terms of the fight against disinformation — and why, for once, there's reason for optimism. Maxim Nitsche builds AI to defend democracies against disinformation. He is the co-founder and CEO of deep, a Berlin-based company whose system, deepTrust, detects coordinated manipulation campaigns before they go viral.

His path started early. At 15, Maxim co-founded MATH 42 with his brother and his father. The AI tutor helped over 7 million students overcome their fear of math at a fraction of the cost of private tutoring, and was acquired by Chegg in 2017. The lesson stayed with him: AI is a tool for good — if it is applied thoughtfully.

title: Can we protect democracy from fake news? | Maxim Nitsche | TEDxBerlin

author: TEDx Talks
description: We humans have bodily awareness that gives us proprioception — but what about robots? Fernando Díaz Ledezma explains how giving robots an inner sense of their body can make them more resilient and adaptive. He further explains why this ability could be a major step forward in enabling robots to truly be able to interact with our world and learn about their self on their own. Fernando Díaz Ledezma is a robotics researcher at the Munich Institute of Robotics and Machine Intelligence (MIRMI) at the Technical University of Munich. His work explores how robots can develop a sense of their own physical body through learning, enabling them to adapt, recover from damage, and interact more naturally with the world. By combining insights from robotics, neuroscience, and embodied intelligence, Fernando is helping shape the next generation of adaptive and resilient machines. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn
title: Why Should Robots Learn Their Physical Self? | Fernando Diaz Ledezma | TEDxTUM

author: TEDx Talks
description: While linguistics is the study of language, the best way to truly learn a language is to live it. Learn language authentically. A senior physics student at Purdue, Aastha Patel bridges scientific inquiry and social impact. Her passion for making knowledge accessible drove her to develop a unique language-learning tool that meets learners where they are. Aastha's work reflects her belief that understanding the universe is only half the journey. The other half is understanding each other. Outside the lab, she can be found reading, solving puzzles, or exploring nature, always curious about what is next. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: To Learn a Language is to Live It | Aastha Patel | TEDxPurdueU

At 19, Juliana was paralysed by a one-in-a-million illness — and years later, nearly deported from New Zealand for the "crime" of being disabled. Instead of asking "why me?", she learned to charge at life's challenges like a rhino and turn every crisis into a chance to serve others. A funny, fierce and deeply moving case for why your hardest moments might just become someone else's survival guide. Juliana Carvalho is an award-winning disability advocate, bestselling author, and inspirational speaker. Born in Brazil, she became paraplegic at 19 and transformed her experience into a mission to drive change.

title: Find the Rhino Inside You: Turning Crisis Into Opportunity  | Juliana Carvalho | TEDxWaihī Beach

author: TEDx Talks
description: Cosa succede quando una comunità decide di trasformare una mobilitazione ambientale in un progetto concreto di rigenerazione? In questo appassionante talk, David Mascali racconta la straordinaria avventura del Patto per il Fiume Simeto, in Sicilia. Partendo da una ferma protesta dei cittadini contro l'installazione di un impianto di rifiuti tossici e di un inceneritore, il territorio ha saputo unire associazioni, cittadini e l'Ateneo di Catania per mappare le proprie fragilità e valorizzare i propri punti di forza. Attraverso la filosofia della «custodia del sogno» ispirata dalla visione di Danilo Dolci, la Valle del Simeto è diventata un laboratorio nazionale di sviluppo sostenibile, contrasto al caporalato e innovazione sociale. Un percorso resiliente capace di trasformare le difficoltà in un'autentica impresa sociale guidata dai giovani, dimostrando il valore profondo della "restanza". title: Dalla protesta alla proposta: il sogno del Simeto | David Mascali | TEDxCatania Salon

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Narayan Acharya shares his inspiring journey from Jumla and his pursuit of creating sustainable buildings that harmonize with Nepal’s natural environment. Through his work, he explores the potential of using local resources, traditional knowledge, and innovative design approaches to build structures with minimal carbon footprints.

He highlights why sustainable architecture is essential in addressing environmental challenges and creating resilient communities, especially in a country like Nepal where climate, geography, and resources play a crucial role in everyday life. Narayan shares what motivated him to rethink conventional construction practices and embrace solutions that are environmentally responsible, culturally connected, and locally sustainable. His journey reflects how thoughtful design can create a balance between people, nature, and the built environment.

title: Ek Parkhal, Ek Bhawan,Ek Samudaya Ekaichoti | Narayan Acharya | TEDxKathmanduUniversity

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Prof. Dr. Rajendra Koju shares his inspiring journey from his early career and medical training to becoming a renowned cardiologist committed to serving the people of Nepal. Through his experiences working with communities and villages across the country, he highlights the challenges many Nepalese face due to limited access to healthcare services and the importance of making healthcare knowledge accessible to all.
Dr. Koju shares his mission of educating and empowering people about heart health through awareness, prevention, and early intervention. Drawing from real-life cardiac stories of his patients, he explains how many people overlook warning signs and ignore symptoms due to a lack of awareness about heart disease. He also shares practical insights on how we can keep our hearts healthy through balanced lifestyles, regular check-ups, proper nutrition, physical activity, stress management, and timely medical attention. title: Story of Healing Hearts | Prof.Dr Rajendra Koju | TEDxKathmanduUniversity

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if a person is not defined by a single identity, but by the emotions and experiences they carry within? 
KU Theatre Group’s *Abhinaya* takes the audience on a profound journey through the human psyche, where one soul encounters sadness, pain, happiness, anger, and the many emotions that shape existence. Through movement, expression, and storytelling, the performance explores the ever-changing nature of identity and the many selves we discover within.
 KU Theatre Group (KUTG) is Kathmandu University's student-led theatre collective dedicated to using performance as a medium for storytelling, creativity, and social reflection. Through original productions, stage plays, and collaborative performances, KUTG empowers students to explore complex ideas, challenge perspectives, and inspire meaningful conversations. The group has showcased its work at university events and public platforms, blending artistic expression with thought-provoking narratives This talk was given at a TEDx event
title: Natak Abhinaya | Kathmandu University Theatre Group | TEDxKathmanduUniversity

More than musical performances, his compositions tell stories evoking emotion, preserving culture, and creating immersive experiences through the timeless voice of the sitar. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Sitar Without Words | Prashadananda Bharti | TEDxKathmanduUniversity

author: TEDx Talks
description: Success is built through persistence long before it becomes visible. Veteran journalist Rishi Dhamala reflects on the hardships, defining moments, and real-life experiences that shaped his career, sharing stories from the frontlines of journalism and the lessons they taught him about resilience, integrity, and public service. Acknowledging the mistakes he has made along the way, he explains why he continues reporting from the field despite leading one of Nepal's largest media houses, and how his commitment to learning, hard work, and serving the nation remains as strong as ever. Rishi Dhamala is one of Nepal's most prominent journalists, broadcasters, and media entrepreneurs, with a career spanning more than three decades across print, radio, television, and digital media. As the Founder and Chairman of Reporters' Club Nepal, he established one of the country's leading platforms for dialogue among political leaders, policymakers, diplomats, business leaders, civil society, and the pre
title: The Journey of a Journalist | Rishi Dhamala | TEDxKathmanduUniversity

description: Innovation begins where bold ideas meet the right opportunities. Prof. Dr. Bim Prasad Shrestha shares the journey of establishing the Nepal Technology Innovation Center at Kathmandu University, the challenges of building a thriving innovation ecosystem, and the transformative role universities play in empowering students to become innovators, entrepreneurs, and drivers of meaningful change. Prof. Dr. Bim Prasad Shrestha is an engineer, researcher, and innovation leader dedicated to advancing technology-driven solutions for sustainable development. As Director of the Nepal Technology Innovation Center (NTIC) and Professor at Kathmandu University School of Engineering, he leads initiatives that bridge academia, industry, and entrepreneurship to transform research into real-world impact. His work spans engineering innovation, technology commercialization, startup incubation, and multidisciplinary research in areas including climate resilience, water resources, and sustainable infrastruct
title: Innovation and University Impact | Prof. Dr. Bim Prasad Shrestha | TEDxKathmanduUniversity

description: Dhruba Adhikari, former CTO and co-founder of one of Nepal's largest fintech companies, shares the deeply personal journey that reshaped his life after his child was diagnosed with autism. Inspired by his experiences as a father, he founded the Sunflower Institute of Autism to champion awareness, inclusion, and support. In this heartfelt talk, he shows how empathy, acceptance, and early intervention can transform the lives of autistic children and their families. Dhruba Adhikari is a technology entrepreneur, fintech innovator, and social impact leader committed to using technology to solve real-world challenges. As Co-Founder and Chief Technology Officer of IME Khalti, he has helped build one of Nepal's leading digital payment platforms, advancing financial inclusion through secure and accessible digital services. description:
How Creativity and Talent Meet India's Home Industry

India has one of the world's largest home industries, consisting of textiles, food, handcrafted products and more. Discover the unique products the home industry consists of and the industry's impact on the daily life of men and women of all backgrounds. Aashna Shah is a junior at Valencia High School enrolled in the International Baccalaureate and Val Tech programs. She is a dedicated member of Chemistry Olympiad, and competes in state and national level competitions in FBLA and Academic Decathlon. Aashna enjoys learning about chemistry and biology and hopes to pursue biomedical engineering. She also loves to learn about Indian traditions and languages, and strives to better understand her roots and culture. In her free time, Aashna likes doing Bollywood dances, reading, sketching, and watching movies, and her motto is to enjoy the little things in life. description:
Most people think AI starts and ends with chatbots. In this talk, Ananya Barjatiya shows how AI is much bigger than that—and how everyday people can begin exploring small, open-source models for creative, real-world projects.

After catching her sister stealing Sour Patch Kids with a custom computer-vision project, Ananya Barjatiya realized that AI is far more than a chatbot. In this talk, she breaks down what AI models actually are and shows how open-source models can be adapted for small, real-world problems. Her talk invites everyday people to stop seeing AI as distant magic and start seeing it as a creative toolkit. Ananya Barjatiya is a senior in Valencia High School’s Val Tech program who works at the intersection of artificial intelligence, storytelling, and youth mental health. She is a voice actor, one of California’s youngest certified yoga teachers, and the founder of Yoga Connect, a science-backed wellness initiative for teens. title: You can train an AI model, too! | Ananya Barjatiya | TEDxValenciaHighSchool

description:
Every year, the Santa Catarina Judiciary receives over 1 million new cases — one every 20 seconds. In this talk, mathematician Filipe Ivo explains how hoses, peas, and electrical outlets reveal the secrets behind the numbers of Justice. Discover how Jurimetrics is transforming the Judiciary from reactive to proactive — arriving earlier in the future of those who need it most. Filipe Ivo is a mathematician, holds a master's degree in quantitative methods in appraisal, and has been a professor for 25 years. With nearly two decades in the Judiciary of Santa Catarina, he serves as planning advisor to the Presidency of the TJSC — convinced that well-used data can help justice reach those who need it most, faster.

description: Boys are not villains — they are boys in the process of growing up without room to feel, without emotional role models, and increasingly exposed to discourses that teach hatred before anyone teaches them love. Carolina Delboni challenges adults to look at boys with more kindness and urgency. Because raising boys with affection isn't optional — it's what can change what comes out in the end. Carolina Delboni is an educator, psychoanalyst, and writer specializing in adolescent behavior. A weekly columnist for Estadão and author of three books, she works at the intersection of education and adolescence in schools and institutions through consulting and lectures. A finalist for the 2024 Jabuti Prize, she believes that information is a tool for personal development and that it is possible — and urgent — to build kinder, more affectionate relationships with young people. title: Meninos Não Nascem Machistas, Eles Aprendem | Carolina Delboni | TEDxBlumenau
